modeReason: Several stories clear the fresh threshold of 8: the CSAM-official story (novelty3 x magnitude3 x breadth2 = 18) and the rogue-AI-agent breach story (novelty2 x magnitude3 x breadth3 = 18) both easily exceed it.
phrase: An app store cracked down on AI apps that create abuse images. That same week, police said the accused maker was a state's own deputy attorney general.
phraseAlternatives: A phone app store banned AI tools that generate abuse images this week. Police say a state's own deputy attorney general was behind exactly that.
One app store moved to block AI-made abuse images. The person police accuse of creating them works as a state's deputy attorney general.
An app store tightened its rules against AI abuse imagery. Police say the accused maker held the job of state deputy attorney general.

brief.concept: An app store blocks AI apps built to create abuse images, the same week police accuse a state's own deputy attorney general of making exactly that.
brief.metaphor: The guard posted at the door turns out to be hiding the same contraband he was told to stop.

brief.composition: Two-panel paper-cutout collage on kraft card. Left panel: a flat paper app-store gate shape stamps a red-paper 'BANNED' tag over a small cut-paper robot icon marked with an X beside it. Right panel: a paper-cutout government official holds up a cut badge shape; a pair of handcuffs rests beside them, each layer casting a soft paper shadow. Keep the only on-image text to the single word BANNED on the stamp.
